Molecular breeding : new strategies in plant improvement 2026-12-01 Medium

Dissecting the genetic architecture for maize prolificacy by combining QTL mapping and genome-wide association study.

This study dissects the genetic basis of maize prolificacy (number of ears per plant) by combining QTL mapping in two recombinant inbred line populations with a genome-wide association study in a diverse panel. The authors identify 13 QTLs and 8 quantitative trait nucleotides, including a stable locus (qP9-2) that contains two candidate genes involved in tissue differentiation. These findings provide genetic targets that could help breeders improve maize grain yield potential.

Nanopore direct RNA sequencing reveals the 2'-O-methylation landscape and SNORD88B-guided FN1 modification in hepatocellular carcinoma.

This study uses nanopore direct RNA sequencing to map the landscape of 2'-O-methylation (Nm) on mRNA in hepatocellular carcinoma, characterizing its distribution and biological roles. It further identifies C/D box snoRNAs, particularly SNORD88B, that guide Nm modification of the FN1 gene, providing a molecular basis for post-transcriptional regulation in HCC.

The authors propose that these methylation signatures could serve as a non-invasive tool for monitoring liver disease progression in AATD patients.

Chromatin compartment shifting is recurrent and associated with epigenetic reprogramming in prostate cancer.

This study integrated Hi-C, ATAC-seq, and transcriptomic data from 18 clinical prostate samples to map A/B chromatin compartments across benign, primary, and castration-resistant prostate cancer. Using a computational framework that corrects for copy number variation and tumor purity, the authors found recurrent shifts from inactive (B) to active (A) compartments in aneuploid tumors, and these shifts were associated with epigenetic reprogramming. The work suggests that 3D genome reorganization is a recurrent feature of prostate cancer progression.

hlafactor: a tool for multi-layer functional annotation of HLA variation.

hlafactor is a new software tool that consolidates multiple layers of HLA functional annotation—classical alleles, amino-acid residues, and higher-level properties like tapasin dependency, cell-surface expression, and NK cell ligand groups—into a single resource. It addresses the current fragmentation of HLA functional data across publications and reference datasets, enabling integrated multi-layer analyses of this highly polymorphic immune region.

DGIdb in 2026: an interoperable resource for the druggable genome.

DGIdb 2026 is an updated open-access knowledgebase that aggregates and normalizes drug-gene interaction data from many sources, now adding three new datasets (Molecular Oncology Almanac, PRISM Repurposing, and Broad Institute Drug Repurposing). The Journal of molecular diagnostics : JMD 2026-11-18 Medium

Multi-centre implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome test for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer.

This multi-centre study reports real-world implementation of a low-coverage whole-genome sequencing assay (SeqOne SomaHRD) for detecting homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer across four European laboratories. Tumours were classified as HRD-positive based on a Genomic Instability score threshold and/or pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants, with the score derived from measures of large-scale genomic alterations and loss of heterozygosity. The work demonstrates that low-coverage WGS can be deployed as a scalable, reproducible HRD testing approach in routine clinical settings.

DeGenRESOLVE: An offline GUI-based automated nanopore sequencing pipeline for viruses with custom rule-based indel and degeneracy resolution.

DeGenRESOLVE is an offline, GUI-based pipeline for analyzing amplicon-based Oxford Nanopore viral resequencing data when a reference genome is available. It automates the workflow and includes custom rule-based resolution of indels and degenerate base calls, addressing the needs of labs with limited internet access or bioinformatics expertise. The tool does not perform de novo assembly but streamlines reference-guided viral consensus generation.

The authors show that epigenome-informed SNP prioritization can enhance the robustness of genomic prediction while potentially reducing genotyping costs. Cell reports methods 2026-11-17 Medium

Auditing the adversarial robustness of genomic foundation models with SafeGenes.

SafeGenes is an evaluation framework that stress-tests genomic foundation models (like ESM) used for variant effect prediction. It shows that adversarial attacks—input-space perturbations, a discrete SNV-reachable HotFlip attack, and a soft-prompt backdoor—can severely degrade model performance, with PGD attacks dropping AUC by over 30 percentage points on cardiomyopathy and arrhythmia datasets. This highlights a critical robustness gap before such models are trusted in clinical genomics.

Disease-modifying therapies in development for post-traumatic epilepsy.

This review evaluates emerging disease-modifying therapies for post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE), a chronic condition affecting 20% of acquired epilepsies that develops after traumatic brain injury. Current antiseizure medications only suppress early seizures but do not prevent epileptogenesis or improve long-term neurological outcomes. The authors critically assess the pathophysiological basis and therapeutic landscape for interventions that could modify disease progression rather than just treat symptoms.

Comparative genomics reveals contrasting candidate adaptive signatures in two ecologically similar plateau fishes.

This study compared the genomes of two ecologically similar plateau fishes, Aspiorhynchus laticeps and Diptychus maculatus, within a 12-species phylogenomic framework to test whether related fishes in similar cold-water plateau environments show comparable genomic adaptations. By integrating orthogroup inference, gene-family turnover, coding-sequence divergence, and chromosome-scale synteny, the authors found contrasting candidate adaptive signatures between the two species. The results suggest that even ecologically similar relatives can take divergent genomic routes to cope with the same environmental challenges.

Topological Data Analysis Identifies Copy Number Variation Subtypes of Bulls Associated with Fertility.

This study applied topological data analysis (TDA) to genome-wide copy number variation (CNV) profiles from 88 bulls, grouping animals by CNV co-occurrence patterns rather than single-locus effects. The resulting CNV-based subgroups were associated with insemination success rate, suggesting that combined CNV signatures—not just individual variants—capture fertility-relevant structure in cattle. It demonstrates a complementary, pattern-based approach to conventional single-variant association for a polygenic trait.

quarTeT after 3 years: toolkit updates and community insights for telomere-to-telomere genome assembly.

quarTeT, a toolkit for telomere-to-telomere genome assembly and characterization, has received a major update improving all four of its modules: contig filtering in AssemblyMapper, a refactored join algorithm in GapFiller, enhanced telomere detection in TeloExplorer, and holocentric chromosome support in CentroMiner.
